headline: Brent down a 4th session, S&P futures +0.7%, 2y yield highest since July 2024
stance: Oil has fallen four sessions and the dot plot still shows another hike. The front end sold off Friday.

news.head: Brent lower a fourth session, longest run since June
news.body: Brent -1.8% and November WTI -2.2% overnight. Hormuz shipments at a six-month high. Saudi Arabia is restoring its East-West pipeline.

news.head: Trump hosts Xi in Washington Thursday
news.body: Summit set for September 24. Staff-level trade talks opened in New York over the weekend. Tariffs, AI and Iran on the agenda.

news.head: Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia did not lift crude
news.body: Missile and drone attacks Saturday. Crude fell regardless. Qatar confirmed an exchange of messages between the US and Iran.

news.head: Dot plot shows one more hike this year
news.body: Twelve of 18 participants see a single further increase, four see two. Warsh again filed no dot of his own.

implications: Crude fell four sessions while the 2-year yield rose. Rates are not trading cheaper oil as disinflation yet.
Nothing on today's US calendar moves rates. The next scheduled tests are Thursday's summit, then PCE and GDP, September 30.

watch.head: Chicago Fed activity index, 8:30
watch.body: The only US release today, and a tier-three one. August national activity.

watch.head: Trump-Xi summit, September 24
watch.body: Arrival Wednesday, bilateral meeting and state dinner Thursday. Trade truce extension, AI and rare earths on the table.

watch.head: Quarter-end funding, September 30
watch.body: Reverse repo balances are near zero. Any pressure at the turn shows up in reserves instead.

watch.head: PCE and GDP, September 30
watch.body: Both at 8:30 that morning. First inflation and growth prints since the September hike.

sections.title: Macro & Rates
bullets: Front end led Friday's selloff. 2- to 5-year yields rose at least 7bp, the long end less.
Real yields did the work. The 10-year breakeven has not moved in three sessions.
No tier-one US data until JOLTS, September 29. Rates trade the summit and quarter-end until then.
sections.positioning: Tuesday's COT: 5-year Treasury specs hit the 100th percentile, up 13 points. Canadian dollar turned extended long, 88th percentile.

sections.title: Equity Markets
bullets: S&P futures +0.66%, Nasdaq-100 +1.04%, Dow +0.72% at 4:46am ET.
Breadth is the narrowest since March. 28.7% of S&P members sit above their 50-day, from 31.3% Thursday.
The index rose Friday while participation fell. Nasdaq futures lead again pre-market.
sections.positioning: VIX specs have been extended short for six weeks, 13th percentile. Standing background, not a new move.

single_name.note: Star Bulk Carriers: eight insiders bought, filed Thursday. Trades above its 200-day, 1.0 days to cover.

sections.title: Credit & Liquidity
bullets: Commercial paper spreads went back to nothing last week. No funding stress heading into quarter-end.
The reverse repo facility is effectively empty. September 30 lands with no cushion there.

ideas.line: 5 open · 1 closed — no hit rate until 10 (too few to mean anything)
